fields.why: The paired-sera 'more than fourfold increase' in anti-PA IgG is the case definition's confirmatory laboratory criterion ('evidence of a fourfold rise in antibodies between acute and convalescent sera', Note *), i.e. lab confirmation of case status, not a comparison of public health outcomes; B's own notes call it 'an interpretive criterion, not a test'.
Follows from the above: the single-patient acute-vs-convalescent titre rise confirms seroconversion and is not an analytic pair comparison.
With no analytic comparison, scale is null; the 'fourfold' ratio is also computed on an acute value of 0 μg/mL against the footnote's 3.7 μg/mL rule, as both readers note.

brief_issues: The brief excludes case-confirming lab tests from procedures but does not say explicitly that a within-patient lab comparison used as a case-definition criterion (paired-sera rise) is not a comparison for analytic_depth/comparison.
